official.deadline_central_display: Financial aid document deadlines: November 15 (Early Action and Early Decision I), January 15 (Early Decision II), February 15 (Regular Decision), March 15 (transfer Early Decision), April 1 (transfer Rolling Decision)
official.deadline_note: The aid document deadline matches the admission round you choose; a complete financial aid application must be submitted by that round's deadline.
official.application_cycle: Aligned to the UChicago first-year admission rounds (Early Action I, Early Decision I/II, Regular Decision)
official.status_note: International applicants apply for financial aid at the time they apply to UChicago for admission, per the official College Admissions and Financial Aid pages.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: "Need-based gift aid from the College is intended to cover tuition and fees as much as possible" and "We are committed to meeting 100% of your demonstrated need with a loan-free financial aid package if you are admitted and applied for funding."
benefits: Loan-free need-based financial aid package meeting 100% of demonstrated need for admitted international first-year students who applied for funding
Nearly $20 million in need-based aid offered to international students over the past four years, strengthened by a recent $35 million gift for international financial aid
International student stipend, depending on demonstrated need, that covers billed charges over and above tuition and fees - food and housing, and travel if applicable
Automatic consideration for partial-tuition merit scholarships (a single lump sum or a renewable annual award) for all first-year applicants, with no additional application
Packages are sized on the full costs of enrolling: tuition, housing, health insurance, a meal plan, and estimates for books and personal expenses
eligibility: First-year international applicant - a non-U.S. citizen and non-U.S. permanent resident - who applies for financial aid at the same time as the admission application
Aid eligibility is fixed at admission: students who do not apply for aid during the admissions process cannot apply later, including during their four years in the College
International transfer students are not eligible for need-based financial aid or merit scholarships
requirements: Complete the Student Financial Aid Worksheet electronically in the UChicago Account - international aid applicants should not submit the CSS Profile or the FAFSA
Upload all financial aid documents through the UChicago Account; the Office of Financial Aid cannot accept emailed documents
Meet the document deadline associated with your admission application round
The Certification of Finances form need not be submitted with the financial aid application
documents: Student Financial Aid Worksheet completed electronically in the applicant's UChicago Account (the only aid form for non-U.S. citizens and non-U.S. permanent residents)
Proof of Family Income: 2025 tax forms, or the home-country equivalent translated into English and converted into U.S. Dollars
If the home country does not require tax filing: an employer statement of annual income and benefits, or bank statements showing recurring salary deposits
Statements of checking, savings and investment account balances, and a statement showing the value of property owned other than the primary home, if applicable
selection_criteria: Need-based aid is determined during the admission process based on demonstrated need; international students who receive it in the first year re-apply in future years
Merit scholarships are considered independently of financial need; only winners are notified, on a rolling basis through the end of April
The vast majority of UChicago aid is need-based, and applicants should not rely on merit scholarships to fund their education
coverage: Gift aid (grants and scholarships) intended to cover tuition and fees as much as possible
International student stipend (need-dependent) for food and housing and travel if applicable, paid via Workday
Packages are built on estimated full costs including tuition, housing, health insurance, a meal plan, books and personal expenses
application_method: Apply for admission to UChicago and for financial aid at the same time
Complete the Student Financial Aid Worksheet online through the UChicago Account
Upload supporting income and asset documents through the UChicago Account
Meet the document deadline for your admission round
official.application_route: Student Financial Aid Worksheet plus income and asset documents uploaded through the UChicago Account alongside the admission application.
official.citizenship_residency: Designed for international applicants who are non-U.S. citizens and non-U.S. permanent residents
official.international_eligibility: Yes - a dedicated need-based aid route for international first-year applicants, with aid awarded regardless of home address
official.duration: Need-based eligibility is determined during the admissions process before the first year; aided students re-apply in each subsequent year of the College
official.description: The University of Chicago commits to meeting 100% of demonstrated need with a loan-free financial aid package for admitted international first-year students who applied for funding, combining gift aid for tuition and fees with a need-based international student stipend for living costs.
official.program_type: Need-based institutional financial aid for international undergraduates, plus partial-tuition merit scholarships

verification.notes: The loan-free 100%-of-need commitment, once-only-at-admissions eligibility rule, merit scholarship terms and the international student stipend mechanics were confirmed on UChicago's own College Admissions and Financial Aid pages on 2026-10-10 (the pages render via JavaScript, so content was taken from the official domain's published pages). fully_funded is not asserted because UChicago states expenses beyond tuition and fees are paid out of pocket or through the need-dependent stipend. No fixed award amount is published.

applicant_utility.summary: The critical UChicago rule is timing: aid eligibility is decided once, during admissions - if you skip the aid application as an applicant, you cannot apply in any later year of the College. International applicants use only the Student Financial Aid Worksheet in the UChicago Account, not the CSS Profile or FAFSA, and upload translated, USD-converted income and asset documents. Gift aid targets tuition and fees; food, housing and travel are paid out of pocket or through a need-dependent international student stipend paid via Workday, so open a U.S. bank account early if you want direct deposit.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International first-year applicants with substantial financial need who can document family income and assets at application time - not transfer students, who are ineligible for aid.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit the aid application together with your admission application - it cannot be added later
Use the Student Financial Aid Worksheet only; do not file the CSS Profile or FAFSA
Translate foreign tax documents into English and convert amounts to U.S. dollars before uploading
Upload everything through the UChicago Account - emailed documents are refused
Transfer applicants: document that you can fully finance your education instead
common_rejection_risks: Missing the aid application at admissions time - a permanent loss of eligibility
Emailing documents instead of uploading them through the UChicago Account
Submitting the Certification of Finances form and assuming it counts toward the aid application
Relying on merit scholarship odds - the vast majority of UChicago aid is need-based
International transfer applicants assuming they qualify for need-based aid or merit scholarships
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Expenses beyond tuition and fees - food, housing and travel to and from Chicago - are paid out of pocket or through the international student stipend if your demonstrated need qualifies.
document_audit: Non-filing parents need an employer statement of annual income and benefits, or bank statements showing recurring salary deposits
Asset verification requires checking, savings and investment statements plus property values other than the primary home
Documents must be in English and in U.S. dollars before upload
The stipend is paid via Workday as a direct deposit (U.S. bank account required) or a mailed paper check
alerts: Aid eligibility is fixed at admission; once awarded, it is re-applied for in each subsequent year
Merit scholarship notifications arrive on a rolling basis through the end of April - silence is not a decision
International transfer students are excluded from both need-based aid and merit scholarships
A recent $35 million gift for international financial aid strengthens the nearly $20 million awarded to international students over the past four years
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the Worksheet and upload documents in the UChicago Account during your admission round; aid is determined with the admission decision and renewed annually.
